question.text: An installation consists of an electric motor which drives a water pump to lift <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>75</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi></math> of water per second to a height of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>, where water is disbursed at negligible speed. If the motor consumes a power of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kW</mi></math>, then what is the efficiency (%) of the installation? [<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>]

solution.text:
Power consumed by the motor

Pmotor=5000 W

Power used in lifting the water

Pwater=mght=75×10×51=3750 W

The efficiency of the motor is

η=PwaterPmotor×100%

η=37505000×100%=75%
